summary: Core fix is correct: passing multi_class=multi_class makes the scoring instance use the same multinomial/ovr probability computation as LogisticRegressionCV, resolving the reported neg_log_loss discrepancy. However the diff also drops the pre-existing fit_intercept=fit_intercept argument, an unnecessary deviation from the issue's suggested fix that a maintainer would ask to restore.

issues.description: The patch replaces `LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=fit_intercept)` with `LogisticRegression(multi_class=multi_class)`, removing the previously-passed fit_intercept argument rather than adding multi_class alongside it (the issue suggested `LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=fit_intercept, multi_class=multi_class)`). In current code this is functionally harmless because the instance's coef_/intercept_ are set manually and .fit() is never called on it, so fit_intercept is unused at predict/score time and tests still pass. But silently dropping a constructor arg is a confusing, regression-prone de
Minimal-correct fix would keep both arguments; omitting fit_intercept makes the intent less clear to future readers who may assume fit_intercept genuinely doesn't matter here.
